findings.element: .b-away against .b-title in every row of .b-measure (all thirteen states, all widths, and the printed sheet)
findings.problem: The distance and the words it names are one line of text and they do not share a baseline. Measured first-baseline delta between .b-away and its .b-title: phone (15px mono / 17px sans) +1px, desk at 1024/1152/1279/1280/1440 (17px mono / 24px sans) -5px, printed sheet (17px mono / 17px sans) +3px. Three surfaces, three different offsets, none of them zero, because .b-away is hung on a single hand-set 'top: 2px' while the two objects carry different leading roles: the figure is --lead-label (1.4) and the title is --lead-head (1.2), so their half-leadings can never agree at any size pairing. At desk the 17px figure floats visibly high against the 24px title - it reads as a superscript rather than a figure on the line. The behaviour gate cannot see it: interaction-check compares .b-away.top with .b-copy.top within 4px (box tops, L2432), and elsewhere it does assert shared ink edges (.b-title/.b-date/.b-grabWord left within 1px, L644), so the alignment discipline exists everywhere except the one pairing that carries the whole idea. audit.mjs grades leading by role and passes, because both values are on the ladder - they are simply the wrong two values to put side by side.
findings.fix: Stop positioning the figure and start aligning it. Make .b-copy a two-column grid instead of hanging .b-away off it: '.b-copy { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 84px minmax(0, 1fr); column-gap: 40px; align-items: first baseline; margin-left: -124px; }' with .b-away as the first cell (text-align: right) and the title/date/control block as the second; at phone width the columns become 76px / minmax(0,1fr) with margin-left: -110px, matching the existing left/width overrides, which can then be deleted along with '.b-away { position: absolute; left; top: 2px; width }' and the per-medium left/width rules at b.css:1283. Keep 'transform: translateY(var(--push))' on the grid container so the figure and the words still travel as one object, and leave .b-tick absolutely positioned and untouched so it stays on the true pixel. Then assert it: add to interaction-check a check that, for every .b-measure row at 390/768/1024/1280/1440 and in print, the first-baseline of .b-away and of .b-title (Range.getBoundingClientRect().bottom of each first character) differ by no more than 0.5px.

findings.element: .b-printLinkUrl on the print keepsake, under the label THE PLAN STAYS ONLINE AT
findings.problem: The keepsake sets the link with 'word-break: break-all; overflow-wrap: anywhere' inside a 28ch (218.4px) measure, so it renders, identically at 390/768/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440: 'https://timeline.signalstu' / 'dio.ie/s/j7Qm2vK4xR9bT1nL6' / 'yH3cW8pZ5sD0aG7fJ4uE2rN9tM'. The company's own domain is cut mid-syllable on the one artifact a person types from - the printed sheet on the wedding morning. This is the paid-for 'mid-word clamp' class from the defect library, reintroduced by the fix for a neighbouring class: the source comment at b.css:1228 says break-all was added because the 43-character token used to wrap with nothing saying the line continued, and the remedy was applied to the whole string instead of to the token. Both gates are blind to it - audit.mjs does not read break points, and interaction-check only asserts that .b-printLinkUrl starts with 'https://' (L1827) and that the token's case survives (L1402).
findings.fix: Break the token, never the host. In render-b.js emit the printed link as two spans inside .b-printLinkUrl: 'https://timeline.signalstudio.ie/s/j7Qm2vK4xR9bT1nL6yH3cW8pZ5sD0aG7fJ4uE2rN9tM'. In b.css change .b-printLinkUrl to 'word-break: normal; overflow-wrap: normal;' and add '.b-printLinkHost { display: block; white-space: nowrap; } .b-printLinkPath { display: block; word-break: break-all; }'. Scheme plus host is 32 mono characters at 13px = 211px and fits the existing 218.4px measure unchanged, so no geometry moves and textContent still starts 'https://'. Apply the same split to .b-linkField on publish, which at 390 currently breaks 'signalstudio.' / 'ie/s/...' and orphans the TLD.

findings.element: .b-stepRead, the owner's confirmation line in the editing sheet
findings.problem: The single sentence that tells the owner what they just did never once sets on one line. Driven at 390 and at 1024/1152/1279/1280/1440, at rest, after -1 x3, after +7 x2 and after undo, it renders in two lines every time: 'Saturday 8 August 2026 ·' / 'in 23 days', 'Wednesday 19 August 2026 ·' / 'in 34 days', and so on. The string is 326-336px of 15px mono against a 310px box at desk and a 332px box on the phone - it misses by a hair and always breaks, and because the nbsp sits before the connector (asserted at interaction-check L2619) the middot is guaranteed to be the last glyph on the line, hanging with nothing after it. text-wrap: balance then splits 24 characters against 10, so the line is neither justified nor deliberately ragged. The gate blessed exactly this: L1147 only requires the last line to be more than a quarter of the widest, and 96/240 passes.
findings.fix: The line always breaks, so set the break rather than suffering it, and drop the connector that is now doing no work. In render-b.js emit the readout as two block children - 'Saturday 8 August 2026in 23 days' - with '.b-stepReadDay, .b-stepReadAway { display: block; }' and remove the '·' and the nbsp before it; keep --size-body and --lead-label so the block height is unchanged and the sheet's reserved band does not move. Update interaction-check L2619 (which asserts the nbsp before '·') to instead assert that no line of .b-stepRead ends on a separator or a word of three characters or fewer, and keep L2329's normalised field/readout comparison, which is unaffected. If the single line is wanted instead, step .b-stepRead down to --size-data (13px); at 39-40 characters that is 304-312px and still fails at desk, so the two-line setting is the safe answer.

findings.problem: Every generated sentence is handed to text-wrap: balance and nothing else, and balance optimises rag evenness, which repeatedly makes it choose the worst joint in the sentence. Three permanent instances, identical at 390/768/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440: the guest's only sentence about the past reads 'The Orchard reserved, 18 April. The' / 'city hotel shortlist is not going ahead.' - a new sentence's article stranded on the previous line, and widening the 46ch measure makes it worse because breaking after 'April.' gives a 212/262 rag while breaking after 'The' gives 227/247, so balance will keep choosing the orphan. On the printed keepsake the ceremonial today reads 'days away on' / 'Thursday' / '16 July 2026' - the preposition ends the line and the weekday sits alone on the next - inside an 84px box with roughly 100px of free paper to its right. The owner's empty state reads 'Everything on this page is measured from' / 'it, so it is the only thing needed to start.' The master already uses U+00A0 correctly inside dates ('18 April', '3 October 2026'); the habit simply stops there.
findings.fix: Extend the nbsp habit from dates to function words. Add a bindShortWords(s) helper next to the date formatters in render-b.js that replaces a space after any word in the closed list [The, A, An, In, On, At, Of, To, By, For, From, the, a, an, in, on, at, of, to, by, for, from, is, it, and, or] with U+00A0 when that word is followed by a further word, and run every generated sentence through it: .b-behindNote, .b-unit, .b-emptyBody, .b-gapNote, .b-endedBody, .b-pressBody. Separately widen the print unit box from 84px to 152px so 'days away on Thursday' sets on one line above '16 July 2026'. Then assert it: add a check that in owner-flight, phone, desk, day, print, publish, owner-empty and ended at 390/768/1440, no rendered line of those six selectors ends on a word from that list.

findings.element: .b-num, .b-when, .b-away and the letterfit grade on the print state
findings.problem: The A4 keepsake changes its own type ramp depending on the browser window it is previewed in. Measured on state=print: under 701px the sheet sets the count at 96px, the ceremonial date at 20px and the gutter figure at 15px; at 701px and above it sets 148 / 30 / 17. The sheet's grid is already container-queried ('@container (min-width: 600px)' on .b-print .b-two), but the sheet's type ramp is viewport-queried ('@media (min-width: 701px)'), so the document's geometry and its type disagree about how wide the document is. The same media query also silently kills '.b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-body) }' at b.css:1255 - equal specificity, later in source - so the printed figure size is set by a rule aimed at the screen and the rule aimed at the sheet is dead at every width that matters. Related and in the same axis: the letterfit ladder declares --track-display-148, --track-title-64 and --track-title-48 with a comment arguing that one letterfit across 64, 96 and 148 is one too few, and then wires none of the three - the 148px desk count renders at -0.04em (the value declared for the 96px phone count) and the 64px empty-state headline renders at -0.035em rather than its own -0.038em.
findings.fix: Move the sheet's raises out of the viewport query and into the container query that already exists: in the '@container (min-width: 600px)' block on .b-print, set '.b-print .b-num { font-size: var(--size-countWide); } .b-print .b-when { font-size: var(--size-title); letter-spacing: var(--track-head); } .b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-lead); }', and exclude .b-print from the sheet raises inside '@media (min-width: 701px)' by scoping those selectors as '[data-medium="sheet"] :not(.b-print) ...' or by re-stating the print values after them. Delete the now-redundant '.b-print .b-away' rule at b.css:1255. In the same pass wire the declared letterfit steps: '.b-num' at --size-countWide takes --track-display-148, '.b-emptyTitle' at --size-card takes --track-title-64, '.b-pressTitle' at --size-figure takes --track-title-48 - or delete the three tokens, because a declared step nothing uses widens the ladder audit.mjs derives from the custom properties and buys the system nothing.

biggestWin: The type system is genuinely declared rather than described. Size, leading, tracking and space are four named ladders bound to the same role words, so a component picks one role and gets all four together - and it holds under measurement: driving all thirteen states at 390/768/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440 found zero off-ramp sizes, zero leading drift and zero letterfit drift across every family-size-role key. The round-6 uppercase monoculture is fixed and is not creeping back: the sub-fifteen mono tier now carries two clearly separated registers (uppercase at 0.16em for labels, mixed case at 0.04em for data) and no screen shows more than three distinct uppercase specs or more than eight instances. Best of all, and unclaimed by either gate: the reading half of the ladder is in rem and it actually works - setting the root to 20px and to 24px at 390 across ten states produced no horizontal overflow and not one clipped text box, with .b-title stepping 17 to 25.5 and the composed display objects holding their stage. Word-safe trimming with the full string preserved and a real U+2026, tabular figures on every number that changes with the unit riding the count's width, three faces and two weights with no exceptions. Everything I have charged for is the last mile - line breaks and baselines - not the system underneath it. That distance is a polish pass of about a day, not a build and not a different decision.
